name: ponytail
description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
one_liner: A add-on for AI coding assistants that nags them to write less code — fewer lines, fewer new files, no gold-plating — which keeps the resulting software cheaper to run and maintain.
buyer: An engineering manager at a startup paying per-token for AI coding tools who wants to cut both the AI bill and the code-review burden from bloated AI-generated pull requests.
business_use_cases: A startup CTO installs it org-wide to cut Claude Code token spend by ~20% based on the project's own published benchmark.
A coding bootcamp uses it to teach students to recognize when an AI is over-engineering a simple feature.
An agency doing fixed-price AI-assisted development uses it to protect margins by shrinking AI output.

money_ideas.idea: The project's own roadmap (a paid 'Ponytail Pro' waitlist) suggests the natural next step: paid team dashboards showing LOC/cost saved per repo.

steal_this: Not much to build on top of a free skill — the fastest move is publishing your own before/after benchmark on a codebase your audience cares about, to build authority and consulting leads.
